Which accounts a subscription receives events from — the same vocabulary as the
`account_relationship` field in every delivered event envelope. One term to ask for
events, the same term to route them on arrival.

* `own` (default) — only your own account.
* `managed` — only accounts you manage (accounts you provisioned). Whether you actually
  receive them also depends on the management relationship granting data visibility; a
  billing-only relationship does not.
* `all` — both.

A delivered event is always `own` or `managed` (never `all`): its
`account_relationship`, alongside `account_id` and `account_external_ref`, tells you
which account it belongs to.

WebhookDeactivationCause.description:
Who turned a subscription off, alongside `active: false`.

* `owner` — you did, through the API or the dashboard. Turn it back on whenever you want.
* `beel` — we did, because the endpoint stopped accepting anything at all for days.
  Reactivating requires the endpoint to pass a test delivery first (`POST
  /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/test`), so you unblock yourself without opening a ticket.

WebhookFailureCause.description:
Why a delivery to your endpoint did not succeed. The `error` field is free text meant for
a human reading a log; this field is the machine-readable counterpart, so a change in
wording never changes your branching.

* `dns` — the endpoint's domain does not resolve.
* `connection` — the connection could not be opened (refused, host unreachable).
* `tls` — the endpoint's TLS certificate is not valid or not trusted.
* `timeout` — the endpoint accepted the connection but did not answer in time.
* `http_client_error` — the endpoint answered 4xx.
* `http_server_error` — the endpoint answered 5xx.
* `invalid_url` — the subscription URL is malformed and has no host to deliver to.
* `forbidden_target` — the URL points to a non-public network address, which we never
  deliver to.
* `unknown` — the failure could not be classified.

New values may be added over time. Treat any value you do not recognise as `unknown`.

active.description: Whether the subscription receives events. Turning it off, or BeeL. pausing it, drops the deliveries still waiting for an automatic retry: they are not sent when it is turned back on, and stay in the delivery log for a manual retry.

account_relationship.description: Which accounts this subscription receives events from. Same field name and values as the `account_relationship` carried by every event envelope.

deactivated_by.description: Who turned this subscription off. Absent while it is active. `beel` means we paused it because the endpoint went 25 consecutive deliveries without a single success over more than 48 hours — reactivating it requires a successful test delivery first.

deactivated_at.description: When the subscription was turned off. Null while it is active.

last_error.description: Last error seen in the current run of failed deliveries — what to fix. Cleared by the first successful delivery, together with the failure count.

last_error_cause.description: Stable code for `last_error`. Cleared alongside it by the first successful delivery.

consecutive_failures.description: Deliveries in a row that never got through. A delivery that exhausted its attempts counts as one. Any successful delivery resets it to zero, so a healthy endpoint with occasional blips stays near zero.

last_used_at.description: Last delivery that succeeded. Null if none ever has.

WebhookEventTypeEnum.description:
Available webhook event types:
- `invoice.issued` — Invoice issued and finalized
- `invoice.email.sent` — Invoice sent by email
- `invoice.pdf.generated` — The PDF of an invoice was (re)rendered, so any copy you cached
  is stale; fetch it again from the PDF endpoint
- `invoice.voided` — Invoice voided
- `recurring_invoice.paused` — A schedule stopped generating on its own (downgrade or a
  permanent generation failure); the invoice it was going to issue will not arrive
- `invoice.schedule_failed` — A scheduled invoice could not be issued on its date and BeeL.
  gave up retrying; it stays in drafts and can be issued by hand once the cause is fixed
- `verifactu.status.updated` — VeriFactu public status changed (see `VeriFactuSubmissionStatus`)
- `account.claimed` — A provisioned account was claimed by its holder
- `company.created` — A company was created inside a provisioned account
- `representation.signed` — Fiscal representation signed for a NIF (production invoicing enabled)

The `account.*` events are delivered only to the **provisioner** that created the
account; a subscription on any other account never receives them.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint URL that will receive webhook POST requests.

events.description: List of event types to subscribe to.

account_relationship.description: Which accounts this subscription receives events from. Defaults to `own`. Same field name and values as the `account_relationship` carried by every event envelope.

delivery_success.description: Whether your endpoint responded with HTTP 2xx.

http_status.description: HTTP status code returned by your endpoint. Null if the connection failed.

error.description: Error message if the delivery failed (timeout, DNS, etc.).

failure_cause.description: Why the delivery failed, as a stable code. Absent when `delivery_success` is true. Branch on this, never on the wording of `error`.

secret.description:
HMAC-SHA256 signing secret. **Only returned on creation and secret rotation.**
Store it securely — it cannot be retrieved again.

test_delivery.description:
Outcome of a one-off signed test delivery sent to your URL as part of creating the
subscription, so you learn whether your endpoint answers without a second call.

It is **best effort and never blocks the subscription**: the subscription in `data`
exists and is active regardless of what this says, and the field is `null` when the
test could not be run at all. A failure here means your endpoint is not ready yet —
typically because you registered before deploying it — not that anything went wrong
with the registration. Only present on creation, never on secret rotation.

WebhookEventAccountRelationship.description:
How `account_id` relates to you: `own` when the event happened in your own account,
`managed` when it happened in an account you manage. `null` when the event is not
scoped to an account.

WebhookEventDataInvoicePdfGenerated.description:
Data payload for `invoice.pdf.generated` events. Just the identity of the invoice: the
document itself is fetched from the PDF endpoint, which mints a fresh pre-signed URL. One
travelling here would expire in five minutes — less than this delivery's own retry window.

invoice_number.description: Null while the document has no number yet (a proforma, a draft).

WebhookEventDataRecurringInvoicePaused.description:
Data payload for `recurring_invoice.paused` events. Only automatic pauses are delivered:
a schedule someone paused on purpose is not news to whoever paused it.

blocker.description:
What blocked the emission, in the same vocabulary the emission API returns (the
`blockers[]` of a 422 `EMISSION_NOT_READY`). Only for `GENERATION_FAILURE`.

WebhookEventDataInvoiceScheduleFailed.description:
Data payload for `invoice.schedule_failed` events. The invoice is not lost: it stays in
drafts, untouched, and can be issued by hand once the cause is fixed.

invoice_number.description: Usually `null`: the number is assigned on emission, and this invoice was never emitted.

customer_name.description: Legal name of the recipient — what identifies a draft that has no number yet.

scheduled_for.description: The date the invoice was due to be issued.

blocker.description:
What blocked the emission, in the same vocabulary the emission API returns (the
`blockers[]` of a 422 `EMISSION_NOT_READY`). It may be absent when the permanent
failure was not a readiness one.

operation.description:
Which record changed status: the registration (`REGISTRATION`) or the cancellation of a
voided invoice (`VOID`). It is the record `verifactu_registration_id` identifies, the
same one `verifactu-records` lists with that `operation`.

previous_status.description:
Status of this registration before the change. Omitted on the first notification of a
registration, because there is no earlier status: the submission was just accepted for
processing (`new_status` is `PENDING`) or it was rejected before reaching the AEAT
(`new_status` is `REJECTED`).

qr_url.description:
AEAT verification URL encoded in the invoice QR code. Set when the registration is
submitted, so it is carried by every later status change, `REJECTED` included.

qr_base64.description:
QR code as base64-encoded PNG for embedding in PDFs. Set when the registration is
submitted, so it does not wait for `ACCEPTED`.

invoice_hash.description:
SHA-256 hash of the registration record, as VeriFactu defines it. Set when the
registration is submitted.

error_message.description:
Human-readable reason for the outcome. When the AEAT reported a remark or an error, it is
the AEAT's own description. When BeeL. decided the outcome (the submission was rejected
before reaching the AEAT, or BeeL. stopped waiting for a final answer), it is a message
written by BeeL., in English.

WebhookEventDataAccountClaimed.description:
Data payload for `account.claimed` events. Delivered only to the provisioner
that created the account. Fetch the authoritative state by `account_id`.

account_id.description: The provisioned account this event refers to.

external_ref.description: Your own identifier for the account, to reconcile against your system.

email.description: Email of the account holder who claimed the account.

WebhookEventDataCompanyCreated.description:
Data payload for `company.created` events. Delivered only to the provisioner
that created the account.

account_id.description: The provisioned account this event refers to.

external_ref.description: Your own identifier for the account, to reconcile against your system.

nif.description: The NIF (tax id) the holder registered.

company_id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the created company.

WebhookEventDataRepresentationSigned.description:
Data payload for `representation.signed` events. Delivered only to the provisioner
that created the account.

account_id.description: The provisioned account this event refers to.

external_ref.description: Your own identifier for the account, to reconcile against your system.

company_id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the company whose fiscal representation was signed.

nif.description: The NIF whose fiscal representation was signed.

signed_at.description: When the fiscal representation was signed (enabling production invoicing for this NIF).

WebhookEvent.description: Payload delivered to your endpoint on every webhook event.

livemode.description: Deprecated in favour of the `TEST`/`PROD` environment vocabulary: `livemode: true` is equivalent to environment `PROD`.

test.description: `true` only for test deliveries triggered from the dashboard.

company_id.description:
Unique identifier (UUID) of the company the event is about, or `null` when the event is
not scoped to a specific company. A single endpoint receives events for every company it
manages; route on this field.

nif.description: NIF of the company the event is about.

account_id.description:
Account the event happened in. For your own events this is your account; for
events of accounts you manage it identifies which one.

account_external_ref.description:
Your own identifier for that account, as supplied when you provisioned it
(`external_ref`). `null` for accounts you did not provision.

events.description: New list of event types to subscribe to.

active.description: Enable or disable the webhook subscription.

account_relationship.description: New set of accounts this subscription receives events from. Same field name and values as the `account_relationship` carried by every event envelope.

webhook_event_id.description: Groups all delivery attempts for the same logical event.

attempt_number.description: Sequential number of this POST within its delivery. Manual retries continue the same sequence, so this can exceed the number of automatic attempts.

http_status.description: HTTP response status code. Null if connection failed.

response_body.description: Body returned by your endpoint, kept for troubleshooting. Stored up to 2048 characters; longer responses are cut and `response_body_truncated` is true.

response_body_truncated.description: True when your endpoint returned more than 2048 characters and `response_body` holds only the beginning of it.

response_body_length.description: Length of the body your endpoint returned, before it was cut. Null for deliveries recorded before this field existed.

error_message.description: Error description for failed deliveries (timeout, connection error, etc.)

payload.description: The JSON payload that was sent (or attempted) to your endpoint.

request_headers.description:
HTTP headers sent to your endpoint with this delivery attempt.
Includes `BeeL-Signature`, `BeeL-Event`, `BeeL-Event-Id`, `BeeL-Delivery-Id`, and `Idempotency-Key`.

RequestLogSummary.description: Summary of an API request (list view).

api_key_id.description: Id of the API key the request authenticated with.

error_code.description: Public error code returned (e.g. INVOICE_NOT_FOUND). Null if the request succeeded.

RequestLogCursorPagination.description: Cursor-based pagination (keyset on _time + request_id). APL does not support cheap offset.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next (older) page. Null if there are no more.

prev_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the previous (newer) page. Null if this is the first.

RequestLogDetail.description: Full detail of a request, including bodies and headers.

request_body.description: Request body (truncated by the ingestor; no sensitive headers).

EmailDeliverySortBy.description:
Email delivery field the list is ordered by: `sent_at` the instant of the attempt,
`status` the delivery status, `email_type` the kind of email.

ApiKeyAuth.description:
Keys are prefixed `beel_sk_`, and each one carries the scopes it was created with: a key
short of the scope an operation needs is answered `403`. The scope an operation requires
is shown next to its title, and the full catalogue lives in the Scopes reference.

Keys are created from the BeeL dashboard. They are secret credentials: do not share them
or commit them to source control.

SessionCookie.name: BEEL_SESSION
SessionCookie.description:
Session Cookie authentication (for browser-based access).

**Note:** This method is primarily used by the web application.
For programmatic access, use API Keys instead.

UnexpectedError.description:
Any status code the operation does not list above. Every operation declares it, so a
generated client always has a branch to fall into and never loses the cause of a failure
it did not anticipate.

This is where the transport-level answers land — `405`, `406`, `415` and `429` — together
with any status a future version of the API starts returning. All of them carry the same
error envelope as the codes listed explicitly, so `error.code` is what tells them apart:
switching on the status code alone is not enough. See «Transport-level errors» in the
API description for when each one is produced.

A `502` carrying `EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR` also lands here: an outbound integration the
operation depends on failed or did not answer in time. It is a transient condition — retry
with the same `Idempotency-Key` where the operation accepts one.

One exception to the envelope: a failure of the network edge that never reaches the
application (`502`, `503`, `504`, `524`) is generated by Cloudflare and its body is not
BeeL's — it may not even be JSON. Treat those as "no answer", and retry.

error.message: Unsupported media type: text/plain. Supported: application/json

Unauthorized.description:
Missing or invalid authentication. Like every other error, `message`/`detail` is
localized according to `Accept-Language` (`es`, `en`, `ca`); defaults to English when the
header is missing or asks for none of those.

error.message: Authentication is required to access this resource

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the rate limit resets

RateLimit-Limit.description: Maximum requests allowed in the window

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Remaining requests in the current window

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the current window resets

error.message: Too many requests. Please try again in 60 seconds.
Internal server error
Invalid request

Forbidden.description:
Authenticated but not allowed. Ten causes, told apart by `error.code`. The list is
**closed**: every 403 this API returns carries one of these ten, so you can branch on
them exhaustively.

- `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` — the credential lacks a scope the operation requires;
  `error.details.missing_scopes` names them as a single comma-separated string (for
  example `"invoices:write,customers:read"`), not as an array; `required_scopes` has the
  same shape and lists every scope the operation needs. Retrying will not help: mint a key
  that holds them.
- `COMPANY_READ_ONLY` — the scope is there, but your access level over that NIF only
  lets you read it.
- `ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN` — the scope is there, but your role over the account,
  or the management relationship you hold over it, does not cover this operation.
- `ACCOUNT_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` — the account is not yours to reach, which is also the answer
  when it does not exist, so existence is never disclosed.
- `ACTIVE_COMPANY_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` — the same, for a NIF: the company in the path, or the
  one named by `BeeL-Active-Company`, is not one this credential may reach — and again,
  this is also the answer when it does not exist.
- `COMPANY_ACCESS_REVOKED` — your access to the NIF was withdrawn while the request was
  already in flight, so the write was rejected and nothing was recorded. Retrying will
  not help until the access is granted again.
- `LIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` — the operation changes the real account and the call came
  from a test API key (`beel_sk_test_…`). Use your live key or the dashboard.
- `FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE` — your subscription does not include the entitlement the
  operation needs; `error.details.feature_code` names it. This gate runs **before** the
  scope gate, so for such an operation you never see `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` first.
- `NO_ACTIVE_ACCOUNT` — the credential does not resolve to an account, so no scope can be
  evaluated against one. Fail-closed, not a permission that can be granted to you.
- `OPERATION_REQUIRES_SESSION` — the operation is available only from the web session; no
  API key and no OAuth2 token can perform it, whatever scopes it holds.

error.message: You do not have permission to access this resource

ValidationError.description:
`VALIDATION_ERROR` — the body parses but a value is not acceptable. `details` is a flat map from
the offending property's name (in the contract's `snake_case`, nested paths joined with a dot,
e.g. `recipient.address.postal_code`) to a message describing what is wrong with it, one entry
per property. When the rejected value is one outside an enum's vocabulary, `details` instead
follows `FieldDeserializationError` (`field`, `invalid_value`, `allowed_values`).

error.message: The provided data is not valid.

InvalidRequestTarget.description:
The request target could not be read as declared, so nothing was looked up. Three causes,
all named in `error.details`: a path or query parameter whose value does not parse as its
type (`VALIDATION_ERROR` — a UUID that is not a UUID, an unknown enum value, an empty
element in a list such as `status=ISSUED,`), a required parameter that was not sent
(`MISSING_PARAMETER`), or a header that is meant to carry an identifier and does not
(`ACTIVE_COMPANY_HEADER_INVALID`). A list parameter sent entirely empty (`status=`) is
not an error: it is the same as omitting it.

The fault is in the target, not in the content — which is what `422` is defined over.

error.message: The parameter 'invoice_id' has an invalid type. Expected: UUID.

UnprocessableQueryParameter.description:
A parameter parsed as its declared type but its value is not one the operation admits:
a `limit` outside its range (`limit=0`, `limit=101`), a `page` under 1, a `cursor` that is
not one this API issued, more keys than the `metadata` filter accepts, a value outside the
supported set. The query was rejected whole and nothing was read.

Where a `400` says the target could not be understood, this says it was understood and
refused. Fix the value — retrying the same query answers the same way.

error.message: Validation constraint violation.

details.limit: must be greater than or equal to 1

InvoiceWriteBadRequest.description:
One of:
- `INVALID_JSON_FORMAT`: the body is not valid JSON, or a property has the wrong type or
  format. `details` follows `FieldDeserializationError`: `field`, `invalid_value` and, where
  there is one, `expected_format`.
- `SIMPLIFIED_INVOICE_EXCEEDS_LEGAL_LIMIT`: a `SIMPLIFIED` invoice whose total, VAT
  included, is above 3,000€. The same answer when the invoice is created and when an edit
  takes it over the cap, whether the edit changes the lines or changes `type` to
  `SIMPLIFIED`. Issue a `STANDARD` invoice with the customer identified instead.

invalid_json_format.summary: A property with the wrong format

error.message: The field 'due_date' has an invalid date format: '2026-03-04fds'. Expected format: YYYY-MM-DD.

NotFound.description:
The resource addressed by the path does not exist, or is not one this credential can see —
the two are answered identically, so existence is never disclosed. `error.code` names the
kind of resource that was missing, so a client can tell which of several ids in a path
failed to resolve:

- `INVOICE_NOT_FOUND` — the `{invoice_id}` (invoices, proformas and their sub-resources).
- `RECURRING_NOT_FOUND` — the `{recurring_invoice_id}`.
- `CLIENT_NOT_FOUND` — the `{customer_id}`.
- `INVOICE_CLIENT_NOT_FOUND` — the `customer_id` referenced by an invoice body does not
  resolve to a customer of the issuing company.
- `PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` — the `{product_id}`.
- `SERIES_NOT_FOUND` — the `{series_id}`.
- `WEBHOOK_SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND`, `DELIVERY_LOG_NOT_FOUND` — the `{webhook_id}` and the
  `{delivery_id}`.
- `NOT_FOUND` — the generic fallback, for the few resources that carry no code of their own.

Some resources declare a more specific `404` response of their own (`CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`,
`MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`, `GRANT_NOT_FOUND`, `INVITATION_NOT_FOUND`, `REQUEST_LOG_NOT_FOUND`); it
is documented on the operation.

A `404` with `ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` is a different answer: the **path itself** does not exist
in this API (a typo in the route, or a resource that was never here). It says nothing about
any resource. When the path exists but not with that method, the answer is `405`, not `404`.

error.message: Invoice not found

UnprocessableEntity.description: Unprocessable entity - validation or business rule error

error.message: Data cannot be processed

StateConflict.description:
The request is well formed but collides with the state that is already there. Three
families, told apart by `error.code`:

- **Uniqueness** — something with that identity already exists (`CLIENT_DUPLICATE`,
  `PRODUCT_DUPLICATE`, `SERIES_CODE_DUPLICATED`, `NIF_ALREADY_REGISTERED`,
  `MEMBER_ALREADY_IN_ACCOUNT`, `INVOICE_DUPLICATE_EXTERNAL_REFERENCE`).
- **Lifecycle** — the transition does not apply from where the resource is
  (`INVOICE_ALREADY_VOIDED`, `PROFORMA_ALREADY_CONVERTED`, `CLIENT_HAS_INVOICES`,
  `RECURRING_ALREADY_ENDED`, `RECURRING_OCCURRENCE_ALREADY_CONSUMED` — the occurrence the
  recurring template points at has already been billed; read its history instead of
  retrying).
  Read the resource before retrying: the state you assumed is not its state.
- **Concurrency and idempotency** — another write got there first
  (`CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION`), or the `Idempotency-Key` you sent is still in flight
  (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PROCESSING`, retry after a moment) or was already used for a
  different body (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH`, use a new key).

error.message: The resource was modified by another request; read it again and retry

InvalidJsonFormat.description:
`INVALID_JSON_FORMAT` — the body is not valid JSON, or a property has the wrong type or format
(a string where a number is expected, a date that does not parse, a malformed UUID, a boolean
that is not `true`/`false`). The `details` object follows `FieldDeserializationError`:
`field`, `invalid_value` and, where there is one, `expected_format` (or `allowed_values`, for a
boolean). A property the operation does not declare is not a format error: it is ignored.

A value outside an **enum**'s vocabulary is not answered here. The property is a well-formed
string that names nothing the operation knows, so it is judged as content: `422`
(`VALIDATION_ERROR`), with the same `FieldDeserializationError` shape in `details`
(`field`, `invalid_value`, `allowed_values`).

error.message: The field 'due_date' has an invalid date format: '2026-03-04fds'. Expected format: YYYY-MM-DD.

CustomerImportRejected.description:
The file was rejected as a whole, before any record was looked at: it is not valid CSV, its
encoding is not UTF-8, required columns are missing, it is over the size limit, or it carries
more records than the operation accepts.

Which one it was travels in `error.code`, and the values behind it in `error.details`:
`missing_headers` and `found_headers` for `MISSING_HEADERS`, `record_count` and
`max_records` for `TOO_MANY_RECORDS`, `file_size_mb` and `max_file_size_mb` for
`CSV_FILE_TOO_LARGE`. A rejection with nothing to quantify carries no `details`.

error.message: Required headers not found: 'telefono', 'direccion_calle'. Headers found: nombre_fiscal, nif, email

ForbiddenMemberManagement.description: Every cause listed under the plain `403` above, plus the one that governs the people of an account: `MEMBER_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, returned when you reach the account but your role in it does not manage its members, invitations or grants. Only an `OWNER` or an `ADMIN` does; a `MEMBER` gets this code, and so does an API key minted by one.

error.message: Only the owner or an admin can manage account members.

MemberNotFound.description: `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` — no member with that id belongs to the account. Membership ids are not shared between accounts, so a member of another account answers the same way.

error.message: No member with that id belongs to this account.

ForbiddenOwnerReserved.description: Every cause listed under the plain `403` above, plus the three that govern a change to a member: `MEMBER_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, when your role in the account does not manage its members (only an `OWNER` or an `ADMIN` does); `OWNER_ROLE_RESERVED`, when the member you act on is an `OWNER` and you are not one, since an `ADMIN` manages members but not owners; and `LIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`, when the call is made with a test API key (`beel_sk_test_…`).

error.message: Only an owner can assign or transfer the owner role.

ForbiddenMemberManagementLiveCredentialR.description: Every cause listed under the plain `403` above, plus the two that govern a change to the people of an account: `MEMBER_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, when your role in the account does not manage its members, invitations or grants (only an `OWNER` or an `ADMIN` does), and `LIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`, when the call is made with a test API key (`beel_sk_test_…`): members, invitations and grants are shared between Test and Live, so changing them is always a real change. Use your live API key or the dashboard.

error.message: This operation changes the real account; it requires a live API key or a dashboard session.

MemberGrantNotFound.description: Two causes, told apart by `error.code`: `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` (no member with that id belongs to the account) and `GRANT_NOT_FOUND` (the member exists but holds no grant over that company).

error.message: The member holds no grant over that company.

ForbiddenSessionOnly.description: Every cause listed under the plain `403` above, plus the one that governs this operation: `OPERATION_REQUIRES_SESSION` — "This operation is only available from the web session; it cannot be performed with an API key or OAuth." It is returned to **every** machine credential, live key included, whatever scopes it holds, and before any other check, so it is not a permission you can be granted and retrying with a different key never helps. The operation is reserved to a signed-in human in the dashboard because a leaked key must not be able to take an account over. From the session, two more: `OWNER_ROLE_RESERVED`, when the session belongs to an `ADMIN`, since only an `OWNER` hands ownership over, and `MEMBER_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, when the session's role does not manage members.

error.message: This operation is only available from the web session; it cannot be performed with an API key or OAuth.

InvitationNotFound.description: `INVITATION_NOT_FOUND` — no member invitation with that id exists in the account, in any state.

error.message: No invitation with that id in this account.

ForbiddenLiveCredentialRequired.description: Every cause listed under the plain `403` above, plus one specific to writes on the account's control plane: `LIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`, returned when the call is made with a test API key (`beel_sk_test_…`). Members, invitations and grants are shared between Test and Live, so changing them is always a real change to the real account — there is no sandbox rehearsal of it. The same applies to changing a managed account's access level and to ending its management: both act on an account that may already be invoicing. Use your live API key or the dashboard; reading these resources keeps working with either key, and so does the whole account provisioning flow (provisioning and claim tokens), which creates an inert account and is what you are meant to rehearse in Test — with your test key, but still only if your subscription carries the `manage_accounts` entitlement: that gate applies in Test exactly as it does in Live, and without it the rehearsal answers `403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE` rather than this code. Accounts that have no live mode manage their people from the dashboard.

error.message: This operation changes the real account; it requires a live API key or a dashboard session.

PayloadTooLarge.description:
Payload too large. On this operation that normally means an uploaded file
exceeded its own limit (`FILE_TOO_LARGE`). Any request may also be
rejected with `REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE` when the body as a whole exceeds
the maximum described under *Request body size*. In both cases the
`details` object carries the applicable maximum.

error.message: The file exceeds the maximum allowed size of 5.0 MB.

SeriesValidationError.description:
The series is rejected. `error.code` is `VALIDATION_ERROR` when the body parses but a value
is not acceptable: `details` is a flat map from the offending property's name (in the
contract's `snake_case`) to a message describing what is wrong with it, or follows
`FieldDeserializationError` when the value is outside an enum's vocabulary. Otherwise it is
one of the series rules, among them:
- `SERIES_MONTHLY_REQUIRES_MONTH_AND_YEAR` / `SERIES_ANNUAL_REQUIRES_YEAR` — the format
  cannot tell the counter reset periods apart.
- `SERIES_INITIAL_NUMBER_OUT_OF_RANGE` — the initial number is out of range.
- `SERIES_FORMAT_NUMBER_TOO_LONG` — the longest number the series can generate (the
  format with the code, the year, the month and the counter substituted) exceeds the 60
  characters the AEAT accepts for the invoice number. The counter counts as at least 9
  digits, with or without padding: `{NUM:X}` is a minimum width and the number keeps
  growing past it.
- `SERIES_FORMAT_INVALID_CHARACTERS` — that number would contain a character the AEAT does
  not accept: only printable ASCII (32-126) is allowed, except `"`, `'`, `<`, `>` and `=`.

error.message: The number this series generates can reach 64 characters and the AEAT accepts at most 60 (series and number together). Shorten the code or the fixed text of the format

PaymentConnectionNotFound.description: `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND` — no connection of this NIF carries this `{connection_id}`. It speaks of the connection, never of the NIF: a NIF you cannot reach answers `403`, while a connection of another NIF answers this same `404` so that naming it reveals nothing.

error.message: Payment connection not found

CompanyNotAccessible.description:
Your account does not own or manage this company. The same answer is given for a
NIF that does not exist.

EventNotOfThisConnection.description:
`CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND` when no connection of this NIF carries this `{connection_id}`;
`EVENT_NOT_FOUND` when the connection is yours but the event is not its own. Both answer
alike to an event that does not exist: the `404` speaks of the connection and the event,
never of the NIF. A NIF you cannot reach answers `403`; a connection of another NIF
answers this `404`, so naming it reveals nothing.

error.message: Payment event not found

WebhookSubscriptionValidationError.description:
The body parses but a value is not acceptable. Branch on `error.code`:

- `VALIDATION_ERROR` — a field fails validation; `error.details` maps each offending
  property to what is wrong with it.
- `URL_MUST_BE_HTTPS` — `url` does not use `https`.
- `WEBHOOK_URL_INVALID` — `url` is not a valid absolute URL.
- `URL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED` — `url` points to an internal network address: a private,
  loopback or link-local range, either as a literal IP or through a host name that
  resolves to one. Use an endpoint reachable from the internet. A host name that does not
  resolve yet is accepted, and deliveries to an internal address are refused anyway.

error.message: The webhook URL points to an internal network address. Use an endpoint reachable from the internet.

UnprocessableRequestLogQuery.description: The query was understood and refused. `error.code` is `REQUEST_LOG_INVALID_CURSOR` when `cursor` is not a cursor this API issued, or `VALIDATION_ERROR` when another query parameter falls outside its declared range. Send the `cursor` exactly as returned by the previous page; a hand-built or truncated value is never accepted.

error.message: The pagination cursor is not valid.

RequestLogNotFound.description: `REQUEST_LOG_NOT_FOUND` — no request log with that correlation identifier is readable: it does not exist, was made by another user, or belongs to the other environment. Which of the three is never disclosed.

error.message: No request log with that identifier is available.

total ÷ quantity. Neither operand is out of range on its own — `total_excluding_tax` is at its
declared maximum and `quantity` declares no minimum at all — so no `maximum` in the contract
can bound the quotient, and it is the quotient that does not fit. The rejection points at the
line and publishes both numbers.
